name: Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg
kurzbeschreibung: The baroque Calvary Church in Imst features a contemplative Way of the Cross, vivid Passion frescoes, and expansive panoramic views.
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily year-round during daylight hours (approx. 08:00–19:00)
beschreibung:
Overview

The baroque Calvary Pilgrimage Church (Wallfahrtskirche Kalvarienberg) rises picturesquely upon a wooded knoll at an elevation of around 890 meters above the historic district capital of Imst in the Tyrolean Oberland. Together with its historic Stations of the Cross and wayside passion chapels, this sacred monument forms a profound spiritual ensemble and a favored scenic destination for locals and travelers alike. From the viewing terrace before the church portal, visitors enjoy an impressive panoramic view across the Imst basin, the Gurgltal and Inntal valleys, and the rugged limestone crags of the Lechtal Alps and the Muttekopf massif.

Route & Requirements

The origins of this revered sanctuary trace back to 1684, when dedicated Imst citizens and local clergy erected a Crucifixion group on the rocky knoll to foster devotion to the Passion. Between 1709 and 1714, the present, widely visible church was constructed under master builder Christian Zangerl. In 1779, the sacred building underwent extensive remodeling and expansion directed by renowned Imst baroque architect Franz de Paula Penz. The architectural silhouette of the hall church is distinguished by a prominent ridge turret with a curved baroque copper dome and a polygonal choir. Inside, visitors are enchanted by colorful late-baroque ceiling frescoes illustrating scenes of Christ's Passion alongside an ornate high altar adorned with life-sized sacred figures. Along the ascending pilgrimage trail, 14 artfully crafted Stations of the Cross with painstakingly restored reliefs line the path leading up the Calvary hill.

Visit & Arrival

The Calvary Church is freely accessible and free of charge during daylight hours year-round (generally open from 08:00 to 19:00). Regular May devotions, Lenten Passion processions, and festive Holy Masses are held here. Arriving by public transport: take ÖBB regional trains to Imst-Pitztal railway station, then continue with VVT city buses directly into downtown Imst (bus stop Imst Stadtplatz or Rathausstraße). From the town center, a signposted walking trail leads in approximately 20 minutes up to the pilgrimage church. By car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 to the Imst exit or via the Fernpass road B189; public parking is available in the town center or near the sports center.

Tips

The walk up the historic Stations of the Cross includes stepped gravel sections and uneven stone paving; sturdy footwear is recommended. Limited vehicular access up to the churchyard is available for visitors with reduced mobility via the rear service lane. Combine your visit with an excursion through the nearby, wild Rosengartenschlucht gorge or a historic walk through the traditional weavers' quarter of Imst.
